- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., +10%+ then -5%+), cap forecast at 1–2 days after peak to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 2–5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.3 in 3 consecutive days.
- If true outcome deviates from forecast by >5% in first 3 days, adjust forecast for next 7 days by aligning with 3-day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by 2–4% in early days, reduce early forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price shows mean reversion, model often fails to correct; apply 1–2% downward bias in forecast if price is above 30-day moving average.
